solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leave Alberta as well as Ontario

parts.note: AB is the standard abbreviation for the Canadian province of Alberta
as well as is another way of saying 'and'
ON is the postal abbreviation for the Canadian province of Ontario

explanation.surface: Someone quits Alberta and Ontario too, leaving Canada behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone or something for good is to desert them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Source of red stains in report of two regular courses

indicators.note: report of means the words are said aloud and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a beat is a regular round, as a policeman walks, and a route is a regular course

explanation.surface: A police report about patrols, with red stains as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' gives the sound of BEAT ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: This root vegetable has deep red juice that stains hands and clothes, so it is a source of red stains.

clue.text: Celtic man rises with bench in revolt

indicators.note: in puts the word for bench inside the reversed name
rises means the name is read upwards in this down entry, so backwards

parts.note: Euan is a Scottish man's name
a bench is a seat

explanation.surface: A Celtic man stands up from his bench in rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns EUAN to NAUE, and 'in' puts SEAT inside it. 'revolt' looks like rebellion but is the verb meaning to disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to sicken or disgust them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Ineptly I carve — not good function of hammer?

indicators.note: ineptly suggests clumsy handling that leaves these letters in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A clumsy carpenter carving badly, missing the point of the hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ineptly' rearranges I CARVE, NOT and G. 'hammer' is not a tool but a ham actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an actor who exaggerates, so a 'hammer' performs in an exaggerated, over-the-top way.

clue.text: Epic fail on first letter

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed after, below the other piece

parts.note: to sag is to weaken or give way
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Slang for a spectacular failure, an 'epic fail', right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Epic fail' reads as modern slang, but 'Epic' is the definition and 'fail' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long heroic story, like the Norse tales, so it is an epic.

clue.text: Ivy League excluded in restrained period

indicators.note: excluded in says the letter for league is removed from the word for restrained

parts.note: held means restrained or kept back
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An elite US university group shut out during a period of restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy League' reads as the American universities, but 'Ivy' is the definition. 'excluded in' takes L out of HELD, leaving HED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the botanical genus name for ivy plants.

clue.text: Wickedness long since hiding every other craziness

parts.note: ill as a noun means evil or wickedness

indicators.note: hiding every other means alternate letters of these words are suppressed, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: Wickedness that has long been concealing a kind of madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding every other' drops L, N, S, N, E from 'long since', leaving OGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of logic is irrational thinking, which is a kind of madness or craziness.

clue.text: Some software cyberattack's not hard, splitting memory block

indicators.note: splitting means the trimmed word breaks the memory block in two

parts.note: a page is a fixed-size block of computer memory

indicators.note: not says the letter for hard is removed from the attack word

parts.note: a hack is a break-in to a computer system
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A computer-security note about a softer cyberattack breaking into memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from HACK, leaving ACK, and 'splitting' puts that inside PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A software bundle of programs sold or installed together is called by this word.

clue.text: Bush began to be difficult over Obama in the end

parts.note: as in 'came to be': things that came about began to be

indicators.note: over signals that the word for difficult is turned round

parts.note: ill can mean difficult or troublesome, as in 'ill-tempered' or 'ill at ease'

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of Obama

explanation.surface: A political grumble: George Bush turned awkward towards Obama at the close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the former president but is the plant. 'over' turns ILL round to LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is an evergreen flowering shrub, so it is an example of a bush.

clue.text: With time guaranteed, though last of students drops out?

definitions.text: With time guaranteed, though last of students drops out?

indicators.note: drops out says a letter is taken away from the word for guaranteed

parts.note: to have ensured something is to have guaranteed it

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of students

explanation.surface: A university post secured for good, even if the final student gives up the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops out' removes S (the end of students) from ENSURED, leaving ENURED after T. The whole clue also describes a lecturer's secure post.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenured academic holds a permanent post, so their time in the job is guaranteed.

clue.text: One more suited to fight than flight is halting tilt

definitions.text: One more suited to fight than flight

parts.note: a game leg is a lame or halting one
to cock your head is to tilt it

explanation.surface: A riddle about a creature built for combat rather than the air, said to be limping at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' here is the old sense of lame, as in a game leg, not sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighting rooster is a bird bred for combat, and such birds barely fly, so it suits a fight more than flight.

clue.text: Naive conjecture surrounds Italian and Spanish articles

indicators.note: surrounds means the conjecture word goes round the two articles

parts.note: a guess is a conjecture
il is the Italian for 'the'
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A trusting soul speculating about grammar in two Romance languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounds' puts IL and EL inside GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without cunning or deceit is innocent and trusting, which is what naive means.

clue.text: American president recalled in hostage troubles

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A US president is reminded of trouble with hostages, like the Iran crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden stretch AGETRO within 'hostage troubles'; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega is president of Nicaragua, a Central American country, so he is an American president in the broad sense.

clue.text: It's macabre holding a cross and putting the feet up

indicators.note: holding means the word for macabre wraps round the other letters

parts.note: something macabre is chilling, so 'it's macabre' describes a chilling thing
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A grim scene of someone gripping a crucifix, set against a picture of lounging about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A and X inside CHILLING.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang blend of chill and relax means unwinding at leisure, which is putting one's feet up.

clue.text: Large string instrument's what I play: it's hard and yellow

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing
the phrase 'I'm on' is how a player says they are performing
the cello is a bowed string instrument

explanation.surface: A musician boasting about a big instrument they play, then a puzzling hard yellow thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'string instrument's what I play' as I'M ON CELLO. 'hard' means strong alcohol, not solid.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian lemon liqueur is a spirit, so a hard drink, and is bright yellow.

clue.text: Trench coat's ten times bigger in the front

indicators.text: ten times bigger in the front
indicators.note: the first letter is the Roman numeral for a hundred; ten times that is the numeral for a thousand, which replaces it

explanation.surface: An oversized trench coat with a huge front.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals C is 100 and M is 1000, so the C of 'coat' grows ten times into M. 'Trench coat' reads as one garment, but 'Trench' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a deep water-filled ditch round a castle, which is a kind of trench.

clue.text: I'm pierced, with deformation of skin

indicators.note: deformation means the letters of these words are twisted out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with piercings complains of disfigured skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deformation' rearranges the letters of 'I'm pierced'.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin, so the adjective describes things relating to the skin.

clue.text: Sporty Spice's 'Goin' Down'? No, somehow it's a climber!

indicators.note: her song title read in a down entry suggests the name going downward the wrong way, so backwards

parts.note: Sporty Spice of the Spice Girls is the singer Melanie Chisholm, known as Mel C

indicators.note: somehow tells you to rearrange these letters in some way

explanation.surface: A pop query: is Mel C's single 'Goin' Down'? No, it's going up, like a climber.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title, in a down entry, sends MELC upward as CLEM; the next indicator rearranges IT'S A into ATIS. The Spice Girls were a British 1990s pop group; 'No' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering vine scrambles up walls and trellises, so it is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Time to stop getting into extra loan

indicators.note: getting into means these letters are placed inside the word for extra

parts.note: more means extra, as in 'some more'
to gag someone is to stop them speaking

explanation.surface: Someone stops borrowing more, or seeks an extra loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts T and GAG inside MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the loan used to buy a house, secured on the property.

clue.text: Mum's graced with singular woman's beauty

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
ma is mum, so mum's is ma's
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A mother with unique grace and feminine beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graced with' just joins the pieces. The answer is British slang for a strikingly attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a stunning person is called this, so it means a beauty.

clue.text: Experience in Munich, and hence

parts.note: und is the German for 'and', the language spoken in Munich
ergo is Latin for therefore or hence

explanation.surface: An experience in a German city, and what follows from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something such as surgery is to experience it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: See where Ruth's found rifle

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
the Book of Ruth is in the Old Testament, abbreviated OT

explanation.surface: A Bible-study instruction to look up where Ruth appears, ending on a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it and steal from it, the same as plundering it.

clue.text: Misunderstanding about rank in married name

indicators.note: in places the words for about and rank between the two abbreviations

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject
a degree is a grade or rank

explanation.surface: Confusion over a title or status when someone takes a spouse's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ONDEGREE between M and N. A mondegreen is a misheard lyric, from 'laid him on the green' heard as 'Lady Mondegreen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a mishearing of a phrase or lyric, a particular kind of misunderstanding.

clue.text: Arousing attraction in the heart (or lower down)?

indicators.note: lower down suggests the whole piece is turned over, reading backwards in this down entry
in puts the word for attraction inside the word for heart

parts.note: the core of something is its heart
'it' is old slang for sex appeal or attraction

explanation.surface: Wondering whether desire lives in the heart or somewhere further south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IT inside CORE to make CITORE, and 'lower down' turns it upside down. The cheeky '(or lower down)' also hints at the body below the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sexually exciting is stimulating, and that is what arousing means here.

clue.text: Orb following celestial object's wake

indicators.note: following puts the letter for orb after the heavenly body

parts.note: a comet is a body that travels through the sky
an orb is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A sphere trailing in the wake of a heavenly body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wake' looks like the trail behind something but is the verb for regaining consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake after fainting is to recover consciousness, which the two-word phrase means.

clue.text: Do resist mixing drugs

indicators.note: mixing tells you to stir up the letters of these words into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid combining drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' rearranges the letters of 'Do resist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are a class of drugs, often misused by athletes, so they are examples of drugs.

clue.text: Jacobi perhaps dismissing one part as rubbish

indicators.note: dismissing one part means one letter of the actor's first name is dropped

parts.note: Sir Derek Jacobi is a famous English actor; 'perhaps' says he is one example of the name

explanation.surface: An actor dropping a role because it was rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing one part' drops an E from DEREK. 'part' looks like a stage role but means a letter. The answer is a Yiddish-derived word.
explanation.definitionFit: This word, borrowed from Yiddish, means trashy worthless stuff, so it means rubbish.

clue.text: Apostle almost having passed in and even out

indicators.note: in puts the word for passed inside the shortened name
almost says the apostle's name loses its final letter

parts.note: St Paul is the apostle to the Gentiles
late can mean passed away, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: An apostle nearly passing in and out, levelling off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PAUL to PAU, and 'in' puts LATE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: When growth levels off it reaches a flat stage, so the verb means to stop rising and stay level.

clue.text: It may help to avoid over-coddling one and get infected with germ

definitions.text: It may help to avoid over-coddling

indicators.note: infected suggests these letters are corrupted and changed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Health advice: avoid over-protecting someone, or they will pick up a germ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infected' rearranges I, GET and GERM. To coddle an egg is to cook it gently in water, so 'over-coddling' means overcooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand timer measures the minutes for boiling an egg, stopping it being overcooked.

clue.text: I'll go red when heated, as one characteristically hitting high?

definitions.meaning: a crustacean whose dark shell turns scarlet when boiled
someone who habitually lobs, sending the ball up high, as in tennis

explanation.surface: A shellfish speaking of its own fate in the pot, then a tennis player known for high shots.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish turns red when cooked, and the second reading is someone who lobs.
